# Monarchs of Sweden since Gustav Vasa — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/swedish-monarchs.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/swedish-monarchs.ttl`](../decks/swedish-monarchs.ttl) · **Cards:** 23 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The 23 monarchs of Sweden from Gustav I (elected 1523) to Carl XVI Gustaf, the two queens regnant included. Front: the monarch's regnal name in English and Swedish; back: the years of the reign, counted from accession to death, abdication or deposition, with the royal house, a short fact and any differing convention in a note. Taken from Wikidata and the public-domain 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica, and checked against the Royal Court's list of monarchs (kungahuset.se).

## Licensing

The content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica, which is in the public domain (published in 1910–1911, so public domain in the United States; most of the articles on the individual kings are by Robert Nisbet Bain, who died in 1909, and the others (Oscar I., Oscar II., Gustavus V.) are unsigned; all were published in 1910–1911). The selection of monarchs, the reign years, the English and Swedish names and the royal houses come from Wikidata, and so do the note facts Wikidata holds; the other note facts come from the 1911 Britannica, in the compiler's own words. So the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The Royal Court's website (all rights reserved), the English Wikipedia list and article (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Svenskt kvinnobiografiskt lexikon (CC BY 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the content sources gave, and no wording, name form, table or selection was taken from them. Facts found only in them were left out of the notes. The one place a verification source is named on a card, the Ulrika Eleonora note saying that the Royal Court's list gives 1719–1720, is a reference to that source's differing year, not content taken from it. The selection is the full set of holders of one Wikidata position since 1523, not a list taken from any of the verification sources.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators, and three independent AI reviewers (factual accuracy; language and translation; licensing, attribution and documentation) whose findings and their resolution are in quality-control rounds 1–3. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Finding the position: the Wikidata search API (query 1 below) returned Q1268572 "Monarch of Sweden". (Two earlier attempts, an exact-label SPARQL lookup and a guess at the current king's item, returned nothing; they are listed in the queries for completeness.)
3. Selection and reign years: a SPARQL query on the Wikidata Query Service (query 4) listed every item with a P39 (position held) statement of Q1268572, with the qualifiers P580 (start time), P582 (end time), P1365 (replaces) and P1366 (replaced by), and the English and Swedish labels. The raw result was saved. Holders with a start time from 1523 on (Gustav I to Carl XVI Gustaf, 23 people, linked into one unbroken chain by the replaces/replaced-by qualifiers) became the cards; Christian II (1520–1521, a union king of Denmark) and the legendary and medieval kings without dates were left out by the brief's scope.
4. Names: query 5 fetched every English and Swedish label and alias of the 23 items, and the Wikidata API (query 6) their English and Swedish Wikipedia sitelink titles. The English front is the conventional English regnal name: the Wikidata label, alias or sitelink title without "of Sweden" (Gustav I from the label "Gustav I of Sweden", Erik XIV, John III, Charles IX … Carl XVI Gustaf; Gustav II Adolf rather than the Latinised Gustavus Adolphus, which is given in the note). The one exception is Sigismund: his Wikidata English label "Sigismund III Vasa" and alias "Sigismund III of Poland" carry his Polish ordinal, so the English front is his Swedish regnal name, the Swedish label "Sigismund", without the ordinal (he was the only Swedish king of that name); the Polish title is in the note. The Swedish front is the Wikidata Swedish label; where that is a by-name, carries a disambiguator or is an older spelling, it is the Swedish alias or label with the disambiguator removed: Gustav I (alias "Gustav I av Sverige"; the label "Gustav Vasa" is the by-name, given in the note), Kristina (label "Kristina av Sverige"; also the alias "Drottning Kristina" without the title) and Gustav IV Adolf (label "Gustaf IV Adolf", alias and sitelink "Gustav IV Adolf"). The Royal Court's list writes the same forms, which confirmed them; no name form was taken from it.
5. Royal houses: query 7 fetched each monarch's P53 (family) and the English and Swedish labels of the five houses; their aliases came from the Wikidata API (query 15). English notes use the Wikidata English labels (House of Vasa, House of Palatinate-Zweibrücken, House of Hesse, House of Holstein-Gottorp, House of Bernadotte). Swedish notes use the Wikidata Swedish labels Vasaätten, Pfalziska ätten and Hessiska ätten, the label "Holstein-Gottorpska ätten (Sverige)" without its disambiguator, and the alias "Ätten Bernadotte" (the Swedish label is just "Bernadotte"). Until quality-control round 3 the Swedish notes wrote "Bernadotteska ätten", the Royal Court's form; it was replaced because the Royal Court is a verification source only.
6. Cross-check: the Royal Court's page "Monarkins historia" (kungahuset.se), whose table "Regentlängd" gives each monarch's period and house, was downloaded and its text extracted (query 8); every card's years were compared with it. The English Wikipedia "List of monarchs of Sweden" (query 9, wikitext through the MediaWiki API) was compared as a second check of the full dates. Where all three agree the card's years are those years. Where they differ (Erik XIV, John III, Ulrika Eleonora; see quality control) the card follows the deck's stated convention and the note names the other year.
7. Convention for the years: a reign runs from accession — succession on the predecessor's death, abdication or deposition, or the monarch's proclamation or election, whichever came first — to the monarch's death, abdication or deposition; coronation dates are not used. Only years are given. The calendar change (Sweden used the Julian calendar until 1753) moves no year boundary in this deck. Karl IX counts from 1604, when he took the title of king; his regency (proclaimed in 1595, sole rule after Sigismund's deposition in 1599) is in the note. Carl XVI Gustaf's reign is written "1973–" because it continues.
8. Notes: each back note names the royal house and, where helpful, one short fact for context (a by-name, a family relation, a regency, the manner of death, the convention used). Every note fact comes from a content source: from Wikidata where it holds the fact as a statement (queries 13–15: parents P22/P25, siblings P3373, spouses P26, dates of birth P569, place and manner of death P20/P1196, positions P39, military rank P410, the house's founder P112, significant events P793 and the item for the assassination of Gustav III), each such statement also a builder check; otherwise from the public-domain 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource (queries 16–17: the articles on the individual kings and the History section of "Sweden"). Ages at accession are computed from Wikidata's date of birth and the start of the reign. Every note fact was then checked against the Royal Court's page and the English Wikipedia list or article. The notes are the compiler's own wording, written directly in English and in Swedish, not copied or closely paraphrased from any source; facts found only in verification sources were left out (Gustaf V's decision not to be crowned, which only the Royal Court gave; the Riksdag's election of Ulrika Eleonora in 1719, which only the Wikipedia list and Svenskt kvinnobiografiskt lexikon gave).
9. Sources tried but not used: Encyclopaedia Britannica online (https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ulrika-Eleonora) answered HTTP 403 (a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." page) to both a fetch tool and curl, and the Nationalencyklopedin article URL tried (https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/ulrika-eleonora-d-y) returned an error page, so neither was consulted and neither is cited. The Royal Court's pages "Sveriges monarki", "Sök" and "Mediecenter" were fetched while looking for the Regentlängd and the site's terms of use; nothing on them was used (query 8b).
10. Machine checks: each card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: P39 = Q1268572 (the person held the position), P53 = the house named in the note, the house's English and Swedish label or alias, the English and Swedish front text where it is exactly a Wikidata label or alias (with the disambiguator, where the front drops one), and every Wikidata statement a note relies on (P22, P25, P3373, P26, P569 year, P20, P1196, P39 King of Poland and Monarch of Norway, P410, P112, P793, and the assassination item's P8032 and P276). The reign years and the end of Oscar II's Norwegian reign are qualifiers, which the builder's checks cannot read; they were checked by queries 4 and 14, whose results are quoted in each card's evidence.

## Selection

Every person Wikidata records as holding the position Monarch of Sweden (Q1268572) with a start date in 1523 or later: Gustav I, elected king in 1523, to the reigning Carl XVI Gustaf, 23 monarchs in all, including the two queens regnant, Kristina and Ulrika Eleonora. Regents who were not monarchs (Gustav Eriksson Vasa as regent before his election in 1523, Duke Karl as regent from 1595 and ruler from 1599 to 1604, the regency governments of Kristina and Karl XI) get no cards of their own; Karl IX's regency is mentioned in his note. Kalmar Union kings (the last, Christian II, 1520–1521) and the medieval and legendary kings are outside the deck's scope. Queens consort are not monarchs and are left out. Front texts are regnal names only; by-names (Gustav Vasa, Gustavus Adolphus) and former names (Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte) appear only in notes.

## Queries

**1. Find the Wikidata item for the position Monarch of Sweden** (Wikidata: holders of the position Monarch of Sweden (Q1268572), with their labels, aliases, sitelinks and family (P53))

```
curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=monarch%20of%20Sweden&language=en&format=json"
```

**2. First attempt to find the position by exact English label (returned no rows)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Monarch of Sweden (Q1268572), with their labels, aliases, sitelinks and family (P53))

```
SELECT ?pos ?posLabel WHERE { ?pos rdfs:label "monarch of Sweden"@en . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". } }
```

**3. Second attempt, via a mistaken item id for the current king (returned no rows)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Monarch of Sweden (Q1268572), with their labels, aliases, sitelinks and family (P53))

```
SELECT ?pos ?posLabel ?n WHERE { wd:Q2721 p:P39 ?st . ?st ps:P39 ?pos . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". } }
```

**4. Every holder of Monarch of Sweden with start, end, predecessor and successor qualifiers (saved as wikidata-p39.tsv)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Monarch of Sweden (Q1268572), with their labels, aliases, sitelinks and family (P53))

```
SELECT ?person ?en ?sv ?start ?end ?endCause ?replaces ?replacedBy WHERE {
  ?person p:P39 ?st .
  ?st ps:P39 wd:Q1268572 .
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1534 ?endCause }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1365 ?replaces }
  OPTIONAL { ?st pq:P1366 ?replacedBy }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?person rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  FILTER(!BOUND(?start) || ?start >= "1500-01-01"^^xsd:dateTime)
}
ORDER BY ?start
```

**5. English and Swedish labels and aliases of the 23 monarchs (saved as wikidata-labels.tsv)** (Wikidata: holders of the position Monarch of Sweden (Q1268572), with their labels, aliases, sitelinks and family (P53))

```
SELECT ?person ?lang ?kind ?text WHERE {
  VALUES ?person { wd:Q52947 wd:Q52945 wd:Q52944 wd:Q52940 wd:Q52939 wd:Q52938 wd:Q52937 wd:Q52936 wd:Q52935 wd:Q52934 wd:Q52933 wd:Q52932 wd:Q52931 wd:Q52930 wd:Q52929 wd:Q52928 wd:Q52927 wd:Q52926 wd:Q52925 wd:Q52924 wd:Q52890 wd:Q52878 wd:Q45068 }
  VALUES ?lang { "en" "sv" }
  { ?person rdfs:label ?text BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?person skos:altLabel ?text BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) = ?lang)
}
ORDER BY ?person ?lang ?kind
```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 33 findings: 30 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 3 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (145 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's years against Wikidata, the Royal Court's list and the English Wikipedia list; names against Wikidata labels and aliases; houses against Wikidata P53. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 23 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata, the Royal Court and Wikipedia agree on the years of 20 of the 23 reigns. Erik XIV/John III (1568 or 1569) and Ulrika Eleonora (1718 or 1719) differ between sources; the cards follow the accession convention stated in the description and the note gives the other year. Several day-level differences inside Wikidata (calendar conversions) leave the years unchanged. Builder checks cover the position (P39), the house (P53), the house labels and every front text that is exactly a Wikidata label or alias; reign years are qualifiers, checked by query 4 instead.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|

| johan-iii | Same discrepancy: Wikidata start 1568-10-10 and the Royal Court 1568–1592, against 26 January 1569 in the English Wikipedia list. | Kept 1568–1592; the note says some lists start at Erik's formal deposition in 1569. | fixed |
| ulrika-eleonora | Wikidata starts the reign on 1718-12-05 and Svenskt kvinnobiografiskt lexikon says she proclaimed herself queen when Charles XII's death became known in 1718; the Royal Court's list gives 1719–1720 and the English Wikipedia list starts on 23 January 1719 (her election by the Riksdag). | Kept 1718–1720 by the accession convention (she took the throne in 1718, before the election); the note says the Royal Court's list gives 1719–1720 and that the Riksdag elected her in 1719. No Wikidata check was skipped: the Wikidata value is the one used. (The election was later removed from the note for want of a content source; see round 3.) | fixed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 23 cards, against the Royal Court's Regentlängd, the Swedish Wikipedia list of regents and article on Karl IX, the English Wikipedia article on Erik XIV and the reviewer's own Wikidata query of the P39 qualifiers.

All 23 reign spans and royal houses correct; the count of 23 confirmed; Ulrika Eleonora's 1718 start judged defensible under the stated convention. Three optional rewordings of notes, all verified against the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica and Wikidata and applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| erik-xiv | The note named only John III as the half-brother who overthrew Erik in 1568; the rising was led by both half-brothers, John and Charles. | Verified: the 1911 Britannica ("Eric XIV.") says "The royal dukes, John and Charles, had already taken measures to depose him", and Wikidata gives both as Erik's siblings by the same father and a different mother. Note now: "Overthrown in 1568 by his half-brothers John (who became John III) and Charles; the Riksdag formally deposed him in January 1569." (sv likewise). Sibling and mother statements added as checks. | fixed |
| karl-ix | The note said "Regent from 1599", leaving out his appointment as regent by the Riksdag of Söderköping in 1595. | Verified: the 1911 Britannica says "In 1595 the Riksdag of Söderköping elected Charles regent" and calls Sigismund's deposition in 1599 a legitimation of his position; the Royal Court counts his regency from 1599. Note now gives both: proclaimed regent in 1595, ruled after Sigismund's deposition in 1599, king from 1604. The back stays 1604–1611; method and selection updated. | fixed |
| gustav-iv-adolf | "Deposed in a coup in 1809, after the loss of Finland" reverses the order: the coup was in March 1809, Finland was ceded at Fredrikshamn in September 1809. | Verified with the 1911 Britannica (king seized on 13 March 1809; Finland given up by the treaty of Fredrikshamn, 17 September 1809). Note now: "Deposed in the coup of 1809, during the Finnish War, which cost Sweden Finland." (sv: "Avsatt genom statskuppen 1809, under finska kriget, som kostade Sverige Finland."), with the Wikidata P793 coup and war statements as checks. | fixed |
